page.text:
A *basis* for a vector space $V$ is a subset $B \subseteq V$ that is
simultaneously linearly independent and spans $V$. A basis represents a
minimal spanning set and a maximal linearly independent set.

Critically, a basis provides a coordinate system: every vector $v \in V$
can be written uniquely as a finite linear combination
$v = \sum_{i=1}^n c_i b_i$ with coefficients $c_i \in F$, establishing a
canonical isomorphism $V \cong F^n$.
